Section C Pronunciation in conversation


                      Exercises

            26.1
                     First match A's questions with B's answers in this conversation. Then look at the B parts and decide
                     whether  the links marked are /w/ links (write /w/) or /j/ links (write /j/).
                       1 | A: Where are you going?
                                                                               B: By_air.
                      2 | A: When?
                                                                               B: Yes, | grew_up there.
                      3 | A: Why?
                                                                               B: Yes, a new_ umbrella.
                      4 | A: Who  is he?
                                                                               B: He_asked  me for one.
                      5  | A: Have you got cousins there, too?
                                                                             .. B:
                      6 | A: How  will you get there?
                                                                               Bi I'll Stay_a week.
                                                                          se |. B: To_ Austria.
                      7 | A: How  long will it take?
                      8 | A: Have you been there before?
                                                                               B: No, they_all live in France.
                      9 | A: How  long will you be there?
                                                                          ome  Bz It's    expensive.
                     10 | A: Why  don't you stay longer?
                                                                          sn   B: To see_ Adam.
                     11 | A: Will you take Adam a present?
                                                                                 A  few_hours.
                     12 | A: Why  an umbrella?
                                                                               B: My_uncle.

               BS7
                     Now  listen and check your answers. Press ‘pause’ before each B part and read it aloud. Then press
                     ‘play’ again and compare your  pronunciation with what  follows.

            26.2
                     Mark  all the possible /r/ links in these sentences containing idiomatic phrases. Say the sentences
                     aloud and  then listen and check your answers. (Check any idioms you don't know  in a dictionary or

            26.3
                     Listen and underline which of the words  you hear in each sentence. As the pairs of words could be
                     pronounced   in a similar way in the sentences, you will need to use the context to help you choose.
               BS9
                     EXAMPLE   held / helped           let / led
                                (She held my  hand  as she led me up the hill.)
                     1  lock / lot                  back  / bat
                     2  play / played               park  / part
                     3  hit / hid                    trick / trip
                     4  like / light
                                                     planned / plan
                                                    road  / robe
                     5  right / ride

                     Now  check  your answers in the Key. Then listen again and repeat the sentences.

                       Follow up: My old English teacher, Mr Brookes, didn't like us to use [r/ links except after words spelt with -r
                       or -re. Which of the links you have marked in exercise 26.2 would Mr Brookes have disapproved of? Do you
                       think Mr Brookes was right in his view of the use of /r/ links?
